2607.24113.title: A Case Study on the Acceptance of a Humanoid Robotic Head Employed in Three Public Spaces
2607.24113.paper_summary: Previous research has shown that a human-like robot's acceptance heavily depends on the setting in which it operates and its ability to perform relevant tasks. This paper, first, reports on how our robot processes natural language to generate a multimodal, verbal response integrating emotional expressions based on an emotion simulation backend. Then, it describes how visitors were invited to speak with our robot in their own language at three different, public locations, where the robot was running continuously for several days. The TAM2 questionnaire results reveal that on average users were motivated to use the robot and found it rather useful and easy to use regardless of the specific location. However, public spaces like the tourist information and the city library seem to be a better fit for our interactive, robotic head than an office environment such as the building authority, where the willingness to interact was lower. Overall, the robot's multi-lingual responses were very much appreciated, but every fifth user found the response time too slow impeding the dialog flow, which remains to be improved in future work.
2607.24113.paper_summary_zh: 先前的研究顯示，人形機器人的接受度在很大程度上取決於其運作的環境以及執行相關任務的能力。本文首先報告了我們的機器人如何處理自然語言，以生成一種多模態的口頭回應，該回應基於情感模擬後端整合了情感表達。接著，描述了如何邀請訪客在三個不同的公共場所用自己的語言與我們的機器人對話，該機器人連續運行了幾天。TAM2問卷的結果顯示，平均而言，使用者有動力使用該機器人，並且無論具體位置如何，都覺得它相當有用且易於使用。然而，像旅遊資訊中心和城市圖書館這樣的公共空間似乎更適合我們的互動機器人頭，而不是像建築管理局這樣的辦公環境，在那裡互動的意願較低。總體而言，機器人的多語言回應受到廣泛讚賞，但每五位使用者中就有一位覺得回應時間過慢，妨礙了對話的流暢性，這在未來的工作中仍需改進。
